aggressive_definition: Lethal prostate cancer among men without cancer at baseline, defined as development of distant organ metastases or death from prostate cancer during follow-up.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: lethal prostate cancer (e.g., men without cancer at baseline who developed distant organ metastases or died from prostate cancer during follow-up)
study_design: Prospective cohort incidence analysis among initially cancer-free men, accompanied by a separate case-only postdiagnosis survival analysis.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Therefore, we prospectively examined total, unprocessed, and processed red meat, poultry, and eggs in relation to risk of lethal prostate cancer (e.g., men without cancer at baseline who developed distant organ metastases or died from prostate cancer during follow-up) among 27,607 men followed from 1994 to 2008.
reason: The incidence analysis explicitly evaluates lethal prostate cancer developing among men without cancer at baseline. The abstract does not report an exposure analysis of total prostate cancer incidence. Its separate analysis among men already diagnosed with nonmetastatic prostate cancer is a survival/progression analysis rather than incidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Men who consumed 2.5 or more eggs per week had an 81% increased risk of lethal prostate cancer compared with men who consumed less than 0.5 eggs per week (HR: 1.81; 95% CI: 1.13-2.89; P(trend): 0.01).
estimate_classifications.reason: This estimate is from the incidence analysis of lethal prostate cancer among men without cancer at baseline.

estimate_classifications.reason: The abstract establishes that total red meat was evaluated in the prospective lethal prostate cancer incidence analysis; the row's numeric estimate comes from supplied full-text evidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: There were suggestive, but not statistically significant, positive associations between postdiagnostic poultry (HR ≥ 3.5 vs. <1.5 servings per week: 1.69; 95% CI: 0.96-2.99; P(trend): 0.07) and postdiagnostic processed red meat (HR ≥ 3 vs. <0.5 servings per week: 1.45; 95% CI: 0.73-2.87; P(trend): 0.08) and risk of progression of localized prostate cancer to lethal disease.
estimate_classifications.reason: This is a postdiagnosis case-only analysis of progression from localized prostate cancer to lethal disease, not incident aggressive prostate cancer among cancer-free men.
